AdGuard 쪽에서 바로 재현하기 좋게 환경 / 재현 방법 / 이미 테스트한 내용 / 로그에서 확인한 점까지 포함해서 작성해봤어. > Subject: Google CAPTCHA appears only in Incognito/Private mode when AdGuard for Mac HTTPS filtering is enabled > Hello AdGuard Support, > I’m experiencing a persistent Google “unusual traffic” CAPTCHA issue when using AdGuard for Mac. > Environment > - AdGuard for Mac: 2.19.0.2258 release > - macOS: 27.0.1 (26A434) > - Network filtering mode: Network Extension / Direct > - Google Chrome: 155.0.8059.26 > - DNS Protection: Disabled > - Stealth Mode: Disabled > - AdGuard Extra: Disabled during testing > - HTTPS Filtering: Enabled > Issue > When AdGuard for Mac is running with HTTPS filtering enabled, Google Search frequently redirects me to the following CAPTCHA page: > https://www.google.com/sorry/... > This happens specifically in: > - Chrome Incognito mode > - Safari Private Browsing > Regular browser sessions generally do not have the same problem. > What I tested > I performed several A/B tests: > 1. AdGuard Desktop + HTTPS filtering ON > - Google CAPTCHA appears in Incognito / Private mode. > 2. HTTPS filtering OFF > - The problem immediately disappears. > 3. AdGuard Desktop completely OFF + AdGuard Chrome Extension ON > - Google Search works normally, even when the extension is explicitly allowed in Incognito mode. > 4. AdGuard Extra OFF > - No change. CAPTCHA still appears. > 5. DNS Protection OFF > - No change. > 6. Stealth Mode OFF > - No change. > 7. Added www.google.com to the HTTPS filtering exclusions > - The CAPTCHA still appeared. > This makes it look like the issue is related specifically to the HTTPS interception/filtering performed by the desktop application rather than an individual browser extension or AdGuard Extra. > Relevant behavior seen in the logs > The logs show that AdGuard intercepts and processes the HTTPS request to Google Search. > For example, the request goes through AdGuard’s SSLFilter and AGHttpProcessingUnit, and AdGuard modifies the response CSP by adding: > local.adguard.org > and an additional nonce. > Shortly afterward, Google responds to another search request with: > HTTP/2 302 > and redirects to: > https://www.google.com/sorry/index?... > The response also includes: > x-hallmonitor-challenge > So the CAPTCHA redirect appears to be generated by Google itself after the request has passed through AdGuard’s HTTPS filtering. > One other detail I noticed is that a request header present before AdGuard processing: > application/signed-exchange;v=b3 > is no longer present in the processed request sent upstream. > Why I think this is related to HTTPS filtering > The strongest indicator is: > - Desktop HTTPS filtering ON → CAPTCHA > - Desktop HTTPS filtering OFF → no CAPTCHA > - Desktop OFF + Chrome Extension ON → no CAPTCHA > So it seems possible that Google’s anti-bot / abuse detection is reacting to something about the HTTPS MITM connection, modified request/response headers, TLS fingerprint, or another characteristic introduced by AdGuard for Mac. > Could you please investigate whether this is a known compatibility issue with Google Search, especially in Incognito/Private browsing sessions? > I can provide the full AdGuard debug logs and state report if needed. > Thank you. ### Screenshots

issue.body:
# ATTENTION

> [!NOTE]  
> YouTube changes their detection scripts regularly. That means that sometime you can face the detection message.
> If all the following instructions do not work, please **email filters@adguard.com** or wait until any update is available. 

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use another adblocker in the same time because using another adblocker can delay/lags the YouTube loading (e.g., AdBlock Plus and AdBlock)[^1] OR interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use an userscript related to the bypassing YouTube detection message like [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing).
> Recently, YouTube anti-adblock script added infinite dummy advertisements to try to neutralize the userscript. ( [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing#264](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing/issues/264) )

> [!WARNING]
> Please check that there no another web browser extension that has adblocking feature is enabled on your web browser. It can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> Saving memory feature of your web browser or sleep feature of your operating system can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.
> In this case, please re-enable AdGuard's filtering by toggling the protection toggle.
> Following the instructions can be needed.

### The instructions
1. Force to update the filters by clicking the reload button in AdGuard Browser Extension/AdGuard mobile or update tray menu in your system tray. [^2]
2. Reload the YouTube webpage without cache by pressing <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd> [^3].
3. Clear cache, cookies and site data of your web browser.
4. Re-open your web browser completely (checking your system monitor[^4] will be better).

[^1]: https://gitlab.com/adblockinc/ext/adblockplus/adblockplusui/-/issues/1576
[^2]: [AdGuard for Windows](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-windows/overview/#tray-menu); [AdGuard for Mac](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-mac/overview/#updates-check); 
[^3]: On macOS, <kbd>Command</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd>
[^4]: Task Manager on Windows, System Monitor on GNOME Shell, KDE System Guard on KDE Plasma or Activity Monitor on macOS. 


Previous issue https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/198973

New change of tinyShield's build script for Apple Safari Extension user (made at 2026 Apr 21) is available.

## Still Have a Problem?
An issue is occurred when the userscript is applied, please report to [this issue tracker](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/issues).

issue.title: ymzu9eeo1y.ru — Yandex Metrica identifier sync on a disguised domain (missed tracker)
issue.body:
### Note on the form
This is a **missed-tracker report**, not a report from an AdGuard installation, so the product/version prerequisites do not apply. Verified against the current AdGuard Tracking Protection (`filters/3.txt`), AdGuard Russian (`filters/1.txt`) and AdGuard DNS-relevant lists on 2026-10-01: no rule matches `ymzu9eeo1y.ru` or the `/wsync/` path. The site contains no sexually explicit material. Same report filed for EasyPrivacy: https://github.com/easylist/easylist/issues/25731

### What product do you use?
n/a (missed-tracker report)

### What type of problem have you encountered?
Privacy — missed tracker (also relevant to DNS filters)

### Which browser(s)?
Safari on iOS (the tracker is served only to iOS Safari-like user agents)

### Where is the problem encountered?
Any site with Yandex Metrica `https://mc.yandex.ru/metrika/tag.js`, e.g. https://bigmike.help/

### Description
Yandex Metrica's `tag.js` loads a JSONP script from `ymzu9eeo1y.ru`, a domain with no visible link to Yandex, to set the identifier cookie `_ym_fa` on the embedding site. The domain resolves to Yandex's own network (`77.88.21.177`, PTR `sync.metrika.yandex.net`) but is registered via REG.RU with Route 53 nameservers and a dedicated certificate, so it is not covered by existing `mc.yandex.*` rules.

The Metrica server returns this URL (as `settings.pic`) only to iOS Safari-like user agents. Blocking it does not break Metrica counting: `tag.js` records `prs=4` and continues.

### Suggested rule
```
||ymzu9eeo1y.ru^
```

### Evidence
```
Domain: ymzu9eeo1y.ru
Suggested rule: ||ymzu9eeo1y.ru^

What it is
- A Yandex Metrica first-party-ID sync endpoint on a domain with no visible link to Yandex.
- A/AAAA: 77.88.21.177 / 2a02:6b8::5b3 — RIPE netname YANDEX-77-88-21-0, org YANDEX LLC ("Yandex enterprise network").
- PTR of 77.88.21.177: sync.metrika.yandex.net
- Registrar REG.RU, created 2024-04-26, no organisation listed; NS on Amazon Route 53 (not Yandex DNS);
  dedicated GlobalSign DV cert (SAN = this name only), continuously reissued since 2024-05 (crt.sh).

Who calls it
- https://mc.yandex.ru/metrika/tag.js (build last-modified 2026-09-22), module "p.suic".
- The URL is NOT hard-coded in tag.js. The Metrica server returns it in the hit response
  (GET https://mc.yandex.ru/watch/<counter>?wmode=7…) as settings.pic, e.g.:
    "pic": "https://ymzu9eeo1y.ru/wsync/5756374941789585625?token=DGIE2fPThYTKhVBGY5e0bvdgQ50KEGaSzZX-BAzOtfw,",
    "ymclid": "5756374941789585625"
  The numeric path segment equals settings.ymclid (Yandex's ID of this specific visit).
- settings.pic is sent only to iOS Safari-like user agents (Mobile Safari, YaBrowser iOS);
  not to Chrome on iOS (CriOS, same WebKit engine), Chrome/Firefox desktop, Chrome Android.
  Tested 2026-10-01: iOS Safari 5/5, YaBrowser iOS 1/1, CriOS 0/1, macOS Safari 0/3,
  Chrome Win 0/1, Firefox Win 0/1, Chrome Android 0/1. (One real-world report also came from macOS Safari 27.)
- It is sent only once per _ym_fa lifetime: if the hit already carries "pic:<_ym_fa>" in browser-info,
  the server omits settings.pic.

What it does
- tag.js injects <script src="https://ymzu9eeo1y.ru/wsync/<ymclid>?token=…&callback=_ymjsp<rand>&wmode=5">.
- Response (JSONP):
    try{_ymjsp…({r:document.referrer,u:location.href,h:"11170.<base64url>.<sig>,"})}catch(e){}
  The response itself reads document.referrer and location.href of the embedding page.
- tag.js then:
    Kd(window, "_ym_fa", h, 43200)            // first-party cookie on the site, 43200 min = 30 days
    ym(<counter>, "params", {__ym: {fsr: referrer, fsu: url}})
  and from then on sends _ym_fa with every hit (qg.pic = cookie "_ym_fa").
- The wsync response also sets a third-party cookie:
    Set-Cookie: _yasc=…; domain=.ymzu9eeo1y.ru; expires=+10 years; SameSite=None; Secure
- Yandex's own cookie documentation describes _ym_fa as "a service cookie that, in combination with the
  _ym_uid cookie, is designed to identify site users" (https://yandex.com/support/metrica/en/general/cookie-usage).

Relevant code (tag.js, de-minified formatting):
    var xA=U("p.suic",function(a,b){return zj(b,function(c){ …
      if(c=J(c,"settings.pic")){ … ki(a,"pic",b)({N:{Cf:!1,fa:["pic"]}},[c]).then(function(l){
        l=l.ib; … var m=l.h; x(m)&&m?(Kd(a,"_ym_fa",m,43200),f("prs",8),k(l)):f("prs",7) … }
    fi.pic=["j"];                                    // JSONP transport
    qg.pic=function(b){return Gd(b,"_ym_fa")};       // cookie value attached to every hit

Why it matters
- mc.yandex.ru / mc.yandex.com are blocked by EasyPrivacy, AdGuard, uBlock, OISD, hagezi, etc.;
  ymzu9eeo1y.ru is in none of them (checked 2026-10-01: EasyPrivacy, EasyList, AdGuard Tracking
  Protection, AdGuard Russian, RU AdList, uBlock filters/privacy, OISD big, StevenBlack, hagezi
  pro/tif/native.yandex, DuckDuckGo TDS, Disconnect). No generic rule matches "/wsync/" either.
- The neutral-looking domain lets Yandex attach a cross-site identifier to visitors exactly in the
  browser (iOS Safari) that tries hardest to prevent that.

Reproduce
  dig +short ymzu9eeo1y.ru A; dig +short -x 77.88.21.177
  curl -s 'https://ymzu9eeo1y.ru/wsync/1?wmode=5&callback=cb'
  curl -s https://mc.yandex.ru/metrika/tag.js | grep -o 'var xA=U("p.suic".\{0,700\}'
  # settings.pic for iOS Safari (creates a hit in the counter you query; use your own counter):
  UA='Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 18_7 like Mac OS X) AppleWebKit/605.1.15 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/26.6.1 Mobile/15E148 Safari/604.1'
  curl -sL -c /tmp/j -b /tmp/j -A "$UA" -H 'Origin: https://<your-site>' \
    'https://mc.yandex.ru/watch/<your-counter>?wmode=7&page-url=https%3A%2F%2F<your-site>%2F&browser-info=ti%3A10' \
    | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["settings"].get("pic"))'
```

issue.body:
# Sorry. The website is infected by AdShield, Inc.

Unfortunately, It is complicated to resolve with a regular adblock rule because the website is being protected by service of Ad-Shield that is an anti-adblock company.

## Userscript Installation
Please block Ad-Shield advertisement by installing [tinyShield userscript](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield).
Please check its installation guideline written in English by visiting [this URL](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.md).

If you can understand Korean language, please refer https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.ko.md.

New change of tinyShield's build script for Apple Safari Extension user (made at 2026 Apr 21) is available.

## Still Have a Problem?
An issue is occurred when the userscript is applied, please report to [this issue tracker](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/issues).

### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking) [https://www.audible.co.jp/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.audible.co.jp%2F) ### Comment > When the AdGuard URL Tracking Filter is enabled, you cannot search for series on Audible (audible.*). You can search for books, but you will be unable to search for series. > > 1. Click the “Search” button and enter the name of your favorite novel series. > 2. Tap the “Series” tab. > 3. Tap the series that appears. > 4. An error page will appear stating that the series does not exist. > > This issue occurs because Audible’s series search redirect uses the `ref` parameter. +app.catchtable.co.kr###popup
comment.body:
This popup returns two local storage keys `CT_POPUP_2062` and `CT_POPUP_2066` when click the "forever hide" button in left side, and the two keys seem to track updates for different promotions.

```adblock
app.catchtable.co.kr#%#//scriptlet('trusted-set-local-storage-item', 'CT_POPUP_2062', 'json:{"value":$currentISODate$,"expiry": 3155761590000}')
app.catchtable.co.kr#%#//scriptlet('trusted-set-local-storage-item', 'CT_POPUP_2066', 'json:{"value":$currentISODate$,"expiry": 3155761590000}')
```

Therefore, It should be simulate the click the hide button.

issue.title: ymzu9eeo1y.ru — Yandex Metrica identifier sync on a disguised domain (missed tracker)

labels.name: A: In progress
labels.description: Work on the issue is in progress

issue.body:
### Note on the form
This is a **missed-tracker report**, not a report from an AdGuard installation, so the product/version prerequisites do not apply. Verified against the current AdGuard Tracking Protection (`filters/3.txt`), AdGuard Russian (`filters/1.txt`) and AdGuard DNS-relevant lists on 2026-10-01: no rule matches `ymzu9eeo1y.ru` or the `/wsync/` path. The site contains no sexually explicit material. Same report filed for EasyPrivacy: https://github.com/easylist/easylist/issues/25731

### What product do you use?
n/a (missed-tracker report)

### What type of problem have you encountered?
Privacy — missed tracker (also relevant to DNS filters)

### Which browser(s)?
Safari on iOS (the tracker is served only to iOS Safari-like user agents)

### Where is the problem encountered?
Any site with Yandex Metrica `https://mc.yandex.ru/metrika/tag.js`, e.g. https://bigmike.help/

### Description
Yandex Metrica's `tag.js` loads a JSONP script from `ymzu9eeo1y.ru`, a domain with no visible link to Yandex, to set the identifier cookie `_ym_fa` on the embedding site. The domain resolves to Yandex's own network (`77.88.21.177`, PTR `sync.metrika.yandex.net`) but is registered via REG.RU with Route 53 nameservers and a dedicated certificate, so it is not covered by existing `mc.yandex.*` rules.

The Metrica server returns this URL (as `settings.pic`) only to iOS Safari-like user agents. Blocking it does not break Metrica counting: `tag.js` records `prs=4` and continues.

### Suggested rule
```
||ymzu9eeo1y.ru^
```

### Evidence
```
Domain: ymzu9eeo1y.ru
Suggested rule: ||ymzu9eeo1y.ru^

What it is
- A Yandex Metrica first-party-ID sync endpoint on a domain with no visible link to Yandex.
- A/AAAA: 77.88.21.177 / 2a02:6b8::5b3 — RIPE netname YANDEX-77-88-21-0, org YANDEX LLC ("Yandex enterprise network").
- PTR of 77.88.21.177: sync.metrika.yandex.net
- Registrar REG.RU, created 2024-04-26, no organisation listed; NS on Amazon Route 53 (not Yandex DNS);
  dedicated GlobalSign DV cert (SAN = this name only), continuously reissued since 2024-05 (crt.sh).

Who calls it
- https://mc.yandex.ru/metrika/tag.js (build last-modified 2026-09-22), module "p.suic".
- The URL is NOT hard-coded in tag.js. The Metrica server returns it in the hit response
  (GET https://mc.yandex.ru/watch/<counter>?wmode=7…) as settings.pic, e.g.:
    "pic": "https://ymzu9eeo1y.ru/wsync/5756374941789585625?token=DGIE2fPThYTKhVBGY5e0bvdgQ50KEGaSzZX-BAzOtfw,",
    "ymclid": "5756374941789585625"
  The numeric path segment equals settings.ymclid (Yandex's ID of this specific visit).
- settings.pic is sent only to iOS Safari-like user agents (Mobile Safari, YaBrowser iOS);
  not to Chrome on iOS (CriOS, same WebKit engine), Chrome/Firefox desktop, Chrome Android.
  Tested 2026-10-01: iOS Safari 5/5, YaBrowser iOS 1/1, CriOS 0/1, macOS Safari 0/3,
  Chrome Win 0/1, Firefox Win 0/1, Chrome Android 0/1. (One real-world report also came from macOS Safari 27.)
- It is sent only once per _ym_fa lifetime: if the hit already carries "pic:<_ym_fa>" in browser-info,
  the server omits settings.pic.

What it does
- tag.js injects <script src="https://ymzu9eeo1y.ru/wsync/<ymclid>?token=…&callback=_ymjsp<rand>&wmode=5">.
- Response (JSONP):
    try{_ymjsp…({r:document.referrer,u:location.href,h:"11170.<base64url>.<sig>,"})}catch(e){}
  The response itself reads document.referrer and location.href of the embedding page.
- tag.js then:
    Kd(window, "_ym_fa", h, 43200)            // first-party cookie on the site, 43200 min = 30 days
    ym(<counter>, "params", {__ym: {fsr: referrer, fsu: url}})
  and from then on sends _ym_fa with every hit (qg.pic = cookie "_ym_fa").
- The wsync response also sets a third-party cookie:
    Set-Cookie: _yasc=…; domain=.ymzu9eeo1y.ru; expires=+10 years; SameSite=None; Secure
- Yandex's own cookie documentation describes _ym_fa as "a service cookie that, in combination with the
  _ym_uid cookie, is designed to identify site users" (https://yandex.com/support/metrica/en/general/cookie-usage).

Relevant code (tag.js, de-minified formatting):
    var xA=U("p.suic",function(a,b){return zj(b,function(c){ …
      if(c=J(c,"settings.pic")){ … ki(a,"pic",b)({N:{Cf:!1,fa:["pic"]}},[c]).then(function(l){
        l=l.ib; … var m=l.h; x(m)&&m?(Kd(a,"_ym_fa",m,43200),f("prs",8),k(l)):f("prs",7) … }
    fi.pic=["j"];                                    // JSONP transport
    qg.pic=function(b){return Gd(b,"_ym_fa")};       // cookie value attached to every hit

Why it matters
- mc.yandex.ru / mc.yandex.com are blocked by EasyPrivacy, AdGuard, uBlock, OISD, hagezi, etc.;
  ymzu9eeo1y.ru is in none of them (checked 2026-10-01: EasyPrivacy, EasyList, AdGuard Tracking
  Protection, AdGuard Russian, RU AdList, uBlock filters/privacy, OISD big, StevenBlack, hagezi
  pro/tif/native.yandex, DuckDuckGo TDS, Disconnect). No generic rule matches "/wsync/" either.
- The neutral-looking domain lets Yandex attach a cross-site identifier to visitors exactly in the
  browser (iOS Safari) that tries hardest to prevent that.

Reproduce
  dig +short ymzu9eeo1y.ru A; dig +short -x 77.88.21.177
  curl -s 'https://ymzu9eeo1y.ru/wsync/1?wmode=5&callback=cb'
  curl -s https://mc.yandex.ru/metrika/tag.js | grep -o 'var xA=U("p.suic".\{0,700\}'
  # settings.pic for iOS Safari (creates a hit in the counter you query; use your own counter):
  UA='Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 18_7 like Mac OS X) AppleWebKit/605.1.15 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/26.6.1 Mobile/15E148 Safari/604.1'
  curl -sL -c /tmp/j -b /tmp/j -A "$UA" -H 'Origin: https://<your-site>' \
    'https://mc.yandex.ru/watch/<your-counter>?wmode=7&page-url=https%3A%2F%2F<your-site>%2F&browser-info=ti%3A10' \
    | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["settings"].get("pic"))'
```

issue.title: ymzu9eeo1y.ru — Yandex Metrica identifier sync on a disguised domain (missed tracker)

labels.name: A: In progress
labels.description: Work on the issue is in progress

issue.body:
### Note on the form
This is a **missed-tracker report**, not a report from an AdGuard installation, so the product/version prerequisites do not apply. Verified against the current AdGuard Tracking Protection (`filters/3.txt`), AdGuard Russian (`filters/1.txt`) and AdGuard DNS-relevant lists on 2026-10-01: no rule matches `ymzu9eeo1y.ru` or the `/wsync/` path. The site contains no sexually explicit material. Same report filed for EasyPrivacy: https://github.com/easylist/easylist/issues/25731

### What product do you use?
n/a (missed-tracker report)

### What type of problem have you encountered?
Privacy — missed tracker (also relevant to DNS filters)

### Which browser(s)?
Safari on iOS (the tracker is served only to iOS Safari-like user agents)

### Where is the problem encountered?
Any site with Yandex Metrica `https://mc.yandex.ru/metrika/tag.js`, e.g. https://bigmike.help/

### Description
Yandex Metrica's `tag.js` loads a JSONP script from `ymzu9eeo1y.ru`, a domain with no visible link to Yandex, to set the identifier cookie `_ym_fa` on the embedding site. The domain resolves to Yandex's own network (`77.88.21.177`, PTR `sync.metrika.yandex.net`) but is registered via REG.RU with Route 53 nameservers and a dedicated certificate, so it is not covered by existing `mc.yandex.*` rules.

The Metrica server returns this URL (as `settings.pic`) only to iOS Safari-like user agents. Blocking it does not break Metrica counting: `tag.js` records `prs=4` and continues.

### Suggested rule
```
||ymzu9eeo1y.ru^
```

### Evidence
```
Domain: ymzu9eeo1y.ru
Suggested rule: ||ymzu9eeo1y.ru^

What it is
- A Yandex Metrica first-party-ID sync endpoint on a domain with no visible link to Yandex.
- A/AAAA: 77.88.21.177 / 2a02:6b8::5b3 — RIPE netname YANDEX-77-88-21-0, org YANDEX LLC ("Yandex enterprise network").
- PTR of 77.88.21.177: sync.metrika.yandex.net
- Registrar REG.RU, created 2024-04-26, no organisation listed; NS on Amazon Route 53 (not Yandex DNS);
  dedicated GlobalSign DV cert (SAN = this name only), continuously reissued since 2024-05 (crt.sh).

Who calls it
- https://mc.yandex.ru/metrika/tag.js (build last-modified 2026-09-22), module "p.suic".
- The URL is NOT hard-coded in tag.js. The Metrica server returns it in the hit response
  (GET https://mc.yandex.ru/watch/<counter>?wmode=7…) as settings.pic, e.g.:
    "pic": "https://ymzu9eeo1y.ru/wsync/5756374941789585625?token=DGIE2fPThYTKhVBGY5e0bvdgQ50KEGaSzZX-BAzOtfw,",
    "ymclid": "5756374941789585625"
  The numeric path segment equals settings.ymclid (Yandex's ID of this specific visit).
- settings.pic is sent only to iOS Safari-like user agents (Mobile Safari, YaBrowser iOS);
  not to Chrome on iOS (CriOS, same WebKit engine), Chrome/Firefox desktop, Chrome Android.
  Tested 2026-10-01: iOS Safari 5/5, YaBrowser iOS 1/1, CriOS 0/1, macOS Safari 0/3,
  Chrome Win 0/1, Firefox Win 0/1, Chrome Android 0/1. (One real-world report also came from macOS Safari 27.)
- It is sent only once per _ym_fa lifetime: if the hit already carries "pic:<_ym_fa>" in browser-info,
  the server omits settings.pic.

What it does
- tag.js injects <script src="https://ymzu9eeo1y.ru/wsync/<ymclid>?token=…&callback=_ymjsp<rand>&wmode=5">.
- Response (JSONP):
    try{_ymjsp…({r:document.referrer,u:location.href,h:"11170.<base64url>.<sig>,"})}catch(e){}
  The response itself reads document.referrer and location.href of the embedding page.
- tag.js then:
    Kd(window, "_ym_fa", h, 43200)            // first-party cookie on the site, 43200 min = 30 days
    ym(<counter>, "params", {__ym: {fsr: referrer, fsu: url}})
  and from then on sends _ym_fa with every hit (qg.pic = cookie "_ym_fa").
- The wsync response also sets a third-party cookie:
    Set-Cookie: _yasc=…; domain=.ymzu9eeo1y.ru; expires=+10 years; SameSite=None; Secure
- Yandex's own cookie documentation describes _ym_fa as "a service cookie that, in combination with the
  _ym_uid cookie, is designed to identify site users" (https://yandex.com/support/metrica/en/general/cookie-usage).

Relevant code (tag.js, de-minified formatting):
    var xA=U("p.suic",function(a,b){return zj(b,function(c){ …
      if(c=J(c,"settings.pic")){ … ki(a,"pic",b)({N:{Cf:!1,fa:["pic"]}},[c]).then(function(l){
        l=l.ib; … var m=l.h; x(m)&&m?(Kd(a,"_ym_fa",m,43200),f("prs",8),k(l)):f("prs",7) … }
    fi.pic=["j"];                                    // JSONP transport
    qg.pic=function(b){return Gd(b,"_ym_fa")};       // cookie value attached to every hit

Why it matters
- mc.yandex.ru / mc.yandex.com are blocked by EasyPrivacy, AdGuard, uBlock, OISD, hagezi, etc.;
  ymzu9eeo1y.ru is in none of them (checked 2026-10-01: EasyPrivacy, EasyList, AdGuard Tracking
  Protection, AdGuard Russian, RU AdList, uBlock filters/privacy, OISD big, StevenBlack, hagezi
  pro/tif/native.yandex, DuckDuckGo TDS, Disconnect). No generic rule matches "/wsync/" either.
- The neutral-looking domain lets Yandex attach a cross-site identifier to visitors exactly in the
  browser (iOS Safari) that tries hardest to prevent that.

Reproduce
  dig +short ymzu9eeo1y.ru A; dig +short -x 77.88.21.177
  curl -s 'https://ymzu9eeo1y.ru/wsync/1?wmode=5&callback=cb'
  curl -s https://mc.yandex.ru/metrika/tag.js | grep -o 'var xA=U("p.suic".\{0,700\}'
  # settings.pic for iOS Safari (creates a hit in the counter you query; use your own counter):
  UA='Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 18_7 like Mac OS X) AppleWebKit/605.1.15 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/26.6.1 Mobile/15E148 Safari/604.1'
  curl -sL -c /tmp/j -b /tmp/j -A "$UA" -H 'Origin: https://<your-site>' \
    'https://mc.yandex.ru/watch/<your-counter>?wmode=7&page-url=https%3A%2F%2F<your-site>%2F&browser-info=ti%3A10' \
    | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["settings"].get("pic"))'
```

issue.title: ymzu9eeo1y.ru — Yandex Metrica identifier sync on a disguised domain (missed tracker)

labels.name: A: In progress
labels.description: Work on the issue is in progress

issue.body:
### Note on the form
This is a **missed-tracker report**, not a report from an AdGuard installation, so the product/version prerequisites do not apply. Verified against the current AdGuard Tracking Protection (`filters/3.txt`), AdGuard Russian (`filters/1.txt`) and AdGuard DNS-relevant lists on 2026-10-01: no rule matches `ymzu9eeo1y.ru` or the `/wsync/` path. The site contains no sexually explicit material. Same report filed for EasyPrivacy: https://github.com/easylist/easylist/issues/25731

### What product do you use?
n/a (missed-tracker report)

### What type of problem have you encountered?
Privacy — missed tracker (also relevant to DNS filters)

### Which browser(s)?
Safari on iOS (the tracker is served only to iOS Safari-like user agents)

### Where is the problem encountered?
Any site with Yandex Metrica `https://mc.yandex.ru/metrika/tag.js`, e.g. https://bigmike.help/

### Description
Yandex Metrica's `tag.js` loads a JSONP script from `ymzu9eeo1y.ru`, a domain with no visible link to Yandex, to set the identifier cookie `_ym_fa` on the embedding site. The domain resolves to Yandex's own network (`77.88.21.177`, PTR `sync.metrika.yandex.net`) but is registered via REG.RU with Route 53 nameservers and a dedicated certificate, so it is not covered by existing `mc.yandex.*` rules.

The Metrica server returns this URL (as `settings.pic`) only to iOS Safari-like user agents. Blocking it does not break Metrica counting: `tag.js` records `prs=4` and continues.

### Suggested rule
```
||ymzu9eeo1y.ru^
```

### Evidence
```
Domain: ymzu9eeo1y.ru
Suggested rule: ||ymzu9eeo1y.ru^

What it is
- A Yandex Metrica first-party-ID sync endpoint on a domain with no visible link to Yandex.
- A/AAAA: 77.88.21.177 / 2a02:6b8::5b3 — RIPE netname YANDEX-77-88-21-0, org YANDEX LLC ("Yandex enterprise network").
- PTR of 77.88.21.177: sync.metrika.yandex.net
- Registrar REG.RU, created 2024-04-26, no organisation listed; NS on Amazon Route 53 (not Yandex DNS);
  dedicated GlobalSign DV cert (SAN = this name only), continuously reissued since 2024-05 (crt.sh).

Who calls it
- https://mc.yandex.ru/metrika/tag.js (build last-modified 2026-09-22), module "p.suic".
- The URL is NOT hard-coded in tag.js. The Metrica server returns it in the hit response
  (GET https://mc.yandex.ru/watch/<counter>?wmode=7…) as settings.pic, e.g.:
    "pic": "https://ymzu9eeo1y.ru/wsync/5756374941789585625?token=DGIE2fPThYTKhVBGY5e0bvdgQ50KEGaSzZX-BAzOtfw,",
    "ymclid": "5756374941789585625"
  The numeric path segment equals settings.ymclid (Yandex's ID of this specific visit).
- settings.pic is sent only to iOS Safari-like user agents (Mobile Safari, YaBrowser iOS);
  not to Chrome on iOS (CriOS, same WebKit engine), Chrome/Firefox desktop, Chrome Android.
  Tested 2026-10-01: iOS Safari 5/5, YaBrowser iOS 1/1, CriOS 0/1, macOS Safari 0/3,
  Chrome Win 0/1, Firefox Win 0/1, Chrome Android 0/1. (One real-world report also came from macOS Safari 27.)
- It is sent only once per _ym_fa lifetime: if the hit already carries "pic:<_ym_fa>" in browser-info,
  the server omits settings.pic.

What it does
- tag.js injects <script src="https://ymzu9eeo1y.ru/wsync/<ymclid>?token=…&callback=_ymjsp<rand>&wmode=5">.
- Response (JSONP):
    try{_ymjsp…({r:document.referrer,u:location.href,h:"11170.<base64url>.<sig>,"})}catch(e){}
  The response itself reads document.referrer and location.href of the embedding page.
- tag.js then:
    Kd(window, "_ym_fa", h, 43200)            // first-party cookie on the site, 43200 min = 30 days
    ym(<counter>, "params", {__ym: {fsr: referrer, fsu: url}})
  and from then on sends _ym_fa with every hit (qg.pic = cookie "_ym_fa").
- The wsync response also sets a third-party cookie:
    Set-Cookie: _yasc=…; domain=.ymzu9eeo1y.ru; expires=+10 years; SameSite=None; Secure
- Yandex's own cookie documentation describes _ym_fa as "a service cookie that, in combination with the
  _ym_uid cookie, is designed to identify site users" (https://yandex.com/support/metrica/en/general/cookie-usage).

Relevant code (tag.js, de-minified formatting):
    var xA=U("p.suic",function(a,b){return zj(b,function(c){ …
      if(c=J(c,"settings.pic")){ … ki(a,"pic",b)({N:{Cf:!1,fa:["pic"]}},[c]).then(function(l){
        l=l.ib; … var m=l.h; x(m)&&m?(Kd(a,"_ym_fa",m,43200),f("prs",8),k(l)):f("prs",7) … }
    fi.pic=["j"];                                    // JSONP transport
    qg.pic=function(b){return Gd(b,"_ym_fa")};       // cookie value attached to every hit

Why it matters
- mc.yandex.ru / mc.yandex.com are blocked by EasyPrivacy, AdGuard, uBlock, OISD, hagezi, etc.;
  ymzu9eeo1y.ru is in none of them (checked 2026-10-01: EasyPrivacy, EasyList, AdGuard Tracking
  Protection, AdGuard Russian, RU AdList, uBlock filters/privacy, OISD big, StevenBlack, hagezi
  pro/tif/native.yandex, DuckDuckGo TDS, Disconnect). No generic rule matches "/wsync/" either.
- The neutral-looking domain lets Yandex attach a cross-site identifier to visitors exactly in the
  browser (iOS Safari) that tries hardest to prevent that.

Reproduce
  dig +short ymzu9eeo1y.ru A; dig +short -x 77.88.21.177
  curl -s 'https://ymzu9eeo1y.ru/wsync/1?wmode=5&callback=cb'
  curl -s https://mc.yandex.ru/metrika/tag.js | grep -o 'var xA=U("p.suic".\{0,700\}'
  # settings.pic for iOS Safari (creates a hit in the counter you query; use your own counter):
  UA='Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 18_7 like Mac OS X) AppleWebKit/605.1.15 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/26.6.1 Mobile/15E148 Safari/604.1'
  curl -sL -c /tmp/j -b /tmp/j -A "$UA" -H 'Origin: https://<your-site>' \
    'https://mc.yandex.ru/watch/<your-counter>?wmode=7&page-url=https%3A%2F%2F<your-site>%2F&browser-info=ti%3A10' \
    | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["settings"].get("pic"))'
```

comment.body: Correction to the list check above: "hagezi pro/tif/native.yandex" should read "hagezi Multi PRO / PRO++ / ULTIMATE and TIF" (there is no native.yandex list). Re-checked the current `wildcard/*-onlydomains.txt` files on 2026-10-01: they block `mc.yandex.ru` but none contains `ymzu9eeo1y.ru`. Also filed there: https://github.com/hagezi/dns-blocklists/issues/11641

comment.body:
The `#popup` name is generic. That could cause false positives in the feature, so I’d like to narrow this rule using :contains, but it doesn’t work with either of the following two rules:

```adblock
app.catchtable.co.kr#%#//scriptlet('trusted-click-element', '#popup button:first-of-type:contains(/^다시 보지 않기$/)')
! or 
app.catchtable.co.kr#%#//scriptlet('trusted-click-element', '#popup button:first-of-type:contains(다시 보지 않기)')
!or 
app.catchtable.co.kr#%#//scriptlet('trusted-click-element', '#popup button:contains(다시 보지 않기)')
```

issue.title: ymzu9eeo1y.ru — Yandex Metrica identifier sync on a disguised domain (missed tracker)

labels.name: A: In progress
labels.description: Work on the issue is in progress

issue.body:
### Note on the form
This is a **missed-tracker report**, not a report from an AdGuard installation, so the product/version prerequisites do not apply. Verified against the current AdGuard Tracking Protection (`filters/3.txt`), AdGuard Russian (`filters/1.txt`) and AdGuard DNS-relevant lists on 2026-10-01: no rule matches `ymzu9eeo1y.ru` or the `/wsync/` path. The site contains no sexually explicit material. Same report filed for EasyPrivacy: https://github.com/easylist/easylist/issues/25731

### What product do you use?
n/a (missed-tracker report)

### What type of problem have you encountered?
Privacy — missed tracker (also relevant to DNS filters)

### Which browser(s)?
Safari on iOS (the tracker is served only to iOS Safari-like user agents)

### Where is the problem encountered?
Any site with Yandex Metrica `https://mc.yandex.ru/metrika/tag.js`, e.g. https://bigmike.help/

### Description
Yandex Metrica's `tag.js` loads a JSONP script from `ymzu9eeo1y.ru`, a domain with no visible link to Yandex, to set the identifier cookie `_ym_fa` on the embedding site. The domain resolves to Yandex's own network (`77.88.21.177`, PTR `sync.metrika.yandex.net`) but is registered via REG.RU with Route 53 nameservers and a dedicated certificate, so it is not covered by existing `mc.yandex.*` rules.

The Metrica server returns this URL (as `settings.pic`) only to iOS Safari-like user agents. Blocking it does not break Metrica counting: `tag.js` records `prs=4` and continues.

### Suggested rule
```
||ymzu9eeo1y.ru^
```

### Evidence
```
Domain: ymzu9eeo1y.ru
Suggested rule: ||ymzu9eeo1y.ru^

What it is
- A Yandex Metrica first-party-ID sync endpoint on a domain with no visible link to Yandex.
- A/AAAA: 77.88.21.177 / 2a02:6b8::5b3 — RIPE netname YANDEX-77-88-21-0, org YANDEX LLC ("Yandex enterprise network").
- PTR of 77.88.21.177: sync.metrika.yandex.net
- Registrar REG.RU, created 2024-04-26, no organisation listed; NS on Amazon Route 53 (not Yandex DNS);
  dedicated GlobalSign DV cert (SAN = this name only), continuously reissued since 2024-05 (crt.sh).

Who calls it
- https://mc.yandex.ru/metrika/tag.js (build last-modified 2026-09-22), module "p.suic".
- The URL is NOT hard-coded in tag.js. The Metrica server returns it in the hit response
  (GET https://mc.yandex.ru/watch/<counter>?wmode=7…) as settings.pic, e.g.:
    "pic": "https://ymzu9eeo1y.ru/wsync/5756374941789585625?token=DGIE2fPThYTKhVBGY5e0bvdgQ50KEGaSzZX-BAzOtfw,",
    "ymclid": "5756374941789585625"
  The numeric path segment equals settings.ymclid (Yandex's ID of this specific visit).
- settings.pic is sent only to iOS Safari-like user agents (Mobile Safari, YaBrowser iOS);
  not to Chrome on iOS (CriOS, same WebKit engine), Chrome/Firefox desktop, Chrome Android.
  Tested 2026-10-01: iOS Safari 5/5, YaBrowser iOS 1/1, CriOS 0/1, macOS Safari 0/3,
  Chrome Win 0/1, Firefox Win 0/1, Chrome Android 0/1. (One real-world report also came from macOS Safari 27.)
- It is sent only once per _ym_fa lifetime: if the hit already carries "pic:<_ym_fa>" in browser-info,
  the server omits settings.pic.

What it does
- tag.js injects <script src="https://ymzu9eeo1y.ru/wsync/<ymclid>?token=…&callback=_ymjsp<rand>&wmode=5">.
- Response (JSONP):
    try{_ymjsp…({r:document.referrer,u:location.href,h:"11170.<base64url>.<sig>,"})}catch(e){}
  The response itself reads document.referrer and location.href of the embedding page.
- tag.js then:
    Kd(window, "_ym_fa", h, 43200)            // first-party cookie on the site, 43200 min = 30 days
    ym(<counter>, "params", {__ym: {fsr: referrer, fsu: url}})
  and from then on sends _ym_fa with every hit (qg.pic = cookie "_ym_fa").
- The wsync response also sets a third-party cookie:
    Set-Cookie: _yasc=…; domain=.ymzu9eeo1y.ru; expires=+10 years; SameSite=None; Secure
- Yandex's own cookie documentation describes _ym_fa as "a service cookie that, in combination with the
  _ym_uid cookie, is designed to identify site users" (https://yandex.com/support/metrica/en/general/cookie-usage).

Relevant code (tag.js, de-minified formatting):
    var xA=U("p.suic",function(a,b){return zj(b,function(c){ …
```

issue.body:
# ATTENTION

> [!NOTE]  
> YouTube changes their detection scripts regularly. That means that sometime you can face the detection message.
> If all the following instructions do not work, please **email filters@adguard.com** or wait until any update is available. 

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use another adblocker in the same time because using another adblocker can delay/lags the YouTube loading (e.g., AdBlock Plus and AdBlock)[^1] OR interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use an userscript related to the bypassing YouTube detection message like [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing).
> Recently, YouTube anti-adblock script added infinite dummy advertisements to try to neutralize the userscript. ( [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing#264](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing/issues/264) )

> [!WARNING]
> Please check that there no another web browser extension that has adblocking feature is enabled on your web browser. It can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> Saving memory feature of your web browser or sleep feature of your operating system can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.
> In this case, please re-enable AdGuard's filtering by toggling the protection toggle.
> Following the instructions can be needed.

### The instructions
1. Force to update the filters by clicking the reload button in AdGuard Browser Extension/AdGuard mobile or update tray menu in your system tray. [^2]
2. Reload the YouTube webpage without cache by pressing <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd> [^3].
3. Clear cache, cookies and site data of your web browser.
4. Re-open your web browser completely (checking your system monitor[^4] will be better).

[^1]: https://gitlab.com/adblockinc/ext/adblockplus/adblockplusui/-/issues/1576
[^2]: [AdGuard for Windows](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-windows/overview/#tray-menu); [AdGuard for Mac](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-mac/overview/#updates-check); 
[^3]: On macOS, <kbd>Command</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd>
[^4]: Task Manager on Windows, System Monitor on GNOME Shell, KDE System Guard on KDE Plasma or Activity Monitor on macOS. 


Previous issue https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/198973

issue.body:
# ATTENTION

> [!NOTE]  
> YouTube changes their detection scripts regularly. That means that sometime you can face the detection message.
> If all the following instructions do not work, please **email filters@adguard.com** or wait until any update is available. 

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use another adblocker in the same time because using another adblocker can delay/lags the YouTube loading (e.g., AdBlock Plus and AdBlock)[^1] OR interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use an userscript related to the bypassing YouTube detection message like [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing).
> Recently, YouTube anti-adblock script added infinite dummy advertisements to try to neutralize the userscript. ( [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing#264](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing/issues/264) )

> [!WARNING]
> Please check that there no another web browser extension that has adblocking feature is enabled on your web browser. It can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> Saving memory feature of your web browser or sleep feature of your operating system can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.
> In this case, please re-enable AdGuard's filtering by toggling the protection toggle.
> Following the instructions can be needed.

### The instructions
1. Force to update the filters by clicking the reload button in AdGuard Browser Extension/AdGuard mobile or update tray menu in your system tray. [^2]
2. Reload the YouTube webpage without cache by pressing <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd> [^3].
3. Clear cache, cookies and site data of your web browser.
4. Re-open your web browser completely (checking your system monitor[^4] will be better).

[^1]: https://gitlab.com/adblockinc/ext/adblockplus/adblockplusui/-/issues/1576
[^2]: [AdGuard for Windows](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-windows/overview/#tray-menu); [AdGuard for Mac](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-mac/overview/#updates-check); 
[^3]: On macOS, <kbd>Command</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd>
[^4]: Task Manager on Windows, System Monitor on GNOME Shell, KDE System Guard on KDE Plasma or Activity Monitor on macOS. 


Previous issue https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/198973

issue.title: Facebooks SONAR logging domains (please read carefullly)
issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] This site DOES NOT contain sexually explicit material, otherwise use [NSFW-specific form](./new?template=bug_report_NSFW.yml);
- [x] Filters were updated before reproducing an issue;
- [x] AdGuard product version is up-to-date;
- [x] Browser version is up-to-date;
- [x] If the site or app is broken, disabling AdGuard protection resolves an issue.

### What product do you use?

AdGuard for Android, AdGuard for iOS

### AdGuard version

*

### What type of problem have you encountered?

Missed analytics or tracker

### Which browser(s) do you use?

the problem is with app, not a site

### Which device do you use?

Mobile

### Where is the problem encountered?

facebook for ios and android

### Ad Blocking

AdGuard Base filter

### Privacy

_No response_

### Social Widgets

_No response_

### Annoyances

_No response_

### Security

_No response_

### Other

_No response_

### DNS filters

_No response_

### Language-specific

_No response_

### What Stealth Mode options do you have enabled?

_No response_

### Add your comment and screenshots

Facebook/Meta appears to be generating an increasingly large number of `sonar` related `fbcdn.net` hostnames.

A collected set currently contains more than **7,000 individual Sonar hostnames**. please see the list here:

https://pastebin.com/TUPCjEG9


 Rather than being random one-off hosts, they follow several highly consistent naming families distributed across Meta's CDN locations.

The main observed patterns include:


sonar.<location>.fna.fbcdn.net
sonar6.<location>.fna.fbcdn.net

sonar-<location>.xx.fbcdn.net
sonar6-<location>.xx.fbcdn.net

edge-sonar-mini-shv-<node>-<location>.fbcdn.net
edge-sonar-mini6-shv-<node>-<location>.fbcdn.net


Examples:


sonar.faae1-1.fna.fbcdn.net
sonar6.faae1-1.fna.fbcdn.net

sonar-iad3-1.xx.fbcdn.net
sonar6-iad3-1.xx.fbcdn.net

edge-sonar-mini-shv-01-atl3.fbcdn.net
edge-sonar-mini6-shv-01-jnb2.fbcdn.net


There is direct evidence from Meta's own `facebook/dns` repository that these domains belong to a dedicated **Sonar** system rather than simply being ordinary static CDN hostnames.

Meta's DNS code contains an `isSonar()` function which identifies a hostname as Sonar when it:

1. ends in `.fbcdn.net`, and
2. contains `sonar` in the hostname.

It also separately recognizes WhatsApp's `.snr.whatsapp.net` Sonar-style domains.

Source:

https://github.com/facebook/dns/blob/9875b2096cd794d436e2af59609d61d5a61db371/dnsrocks/logger/utils.go

Meta's DNS logger also treats Sonar queries differently from ordinary DNS requests. The code explicitly states:

> We only sample non-sonar names

The relevant condition is:

```go
if localRand.Float64() > l.samplingRate && !isSonar(state) {
    return
}
```

This means requests classified as Sonar bypass the normal sampling exclusion applied to non-Sonar names and continue through the DNS logging path.

The logger records information including the query address, response address, query time, and DNS query message.

Source:

https://github.com/facebook/dns/blob/9875b2096cd794d436e2af59609d61d5a61db371/dnsrocks/logger/dnstap_logger.go

Meta's own tests also contain explicit Sonar hostname examples such as:

```text
f41366ce340-kdywlzry1535569283-sonar.xy.fbcdn.net
f41366ce340-kdywlzry1535569283-sonar.snr.fbcdn.net
f3d77e02580klz54ggi-uavvfioa1427990455-sonar.snr.fbcdn.net
fd45417ba30KDACNUXI-fgeytrfl1427990452-sonar.2914.fna.fbcdn.net
```

This confirms that these randomized-looking `*-sonar.*.fbcdn.net` hostnames are deliberately recognized as part of Meta's Sonar infrastructure.

Source:

https://github.com/facebook/dns/blob/9875b2096cd794d436e2af59609d61d5a61db371/dnsrocks/logger/dnstap_logger_test.go

Based on the available evidence, these hosts appear to be associated with **network telemetry, measurement, or diagnostics** rather than ordinary Facebook/Instagram image and video CDN delivery.

The scale is becoming difficult to handle using individual hostname rules. Thousands of location-specific Sonar hosts already exist, and additional CDN locations or node variants can generate more hostnames while retaining the same basic naming structure.

For that reason, I think it would make more sense to block the Sonar hostname family using a generic filtering rule

Conceptually:


suggested filter: * sonar * .fbcdn.net^


Interestingly, this is also very close to Meta's own internal detection logic, which considers an `.fbcdn.net` hostname containing `sonar` to be a Sonar domain.

A generic rule would target the dedicated Sonar infrastructure while avoiding a broad block of `fbcdn.net`, which could interfere with legitimate Facebook and Instagram CDN traffic.

I think these domains are strong candidates for classification as **Facebook/Meta telemetry or network-measurement endpoints** and for inclusion in the **AdGuard DNS filter**.


### Privacy

- [x] I agree to follow this condition

issue.body:
# ATTENTION

> [!NOTE]  
> YouTube changes their detection scripts regularly. That means that sometime you can face the detection message.
> If all the following instructions do not work, please **email filters@adguard.com** or wait until any update is available. 

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use another adblocker in the same time because using another adblocker can delay/lags the YouTube loading (e.g., AdBlock Plus and AdBlock)[^1] OR interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use an userscript related to the bypassing YouTube detection message like [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing).
> Recently, YouTube anti-adblock script added infinite dummy advertisements to try to neutralize the userscript. ( [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing#264](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing/issues/264) )

> [!WARNING]
> Please check that there no another web browser extension that has adblocking feature is enabled on your web browser. It can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> Saving memory feature of your web browser or sleep feature of your operating system can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.
> In this case, please re-enable AdGuard's filtering by toggling the protection toggle.
> Following the instructions can be needed.

### The instructions
1. Force to update the filters by clicking the reload button in AdGuard Browser Extension/AdGuard mobile or update tray menu in your system tray. [^2]
2. Reload the YouTube webpage without cache by pressing <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd> [^3].
3. Clear cache, cookies and site data of your web browser.
4. Re-open your web browser completely (checking your system monitor[^4] will be better).

[^1]: https://gitlab.com/adblockinc/ext/adblockplus/adblockplusui/-/issues/1576
[^2]: [AdGuard for Windows](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-windows/overview/#tray-menu); [AdGuard for Mac](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-mac/overview/#updates-check); 
[^3]: On macOS, <kbd>Command</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd>
[^4]: Task Manager on Windows, System Monitor on GNOME Shell, KDE System Guard on KDE Plasma or Activity Monitor on macOS.

> Yes, the same hang happens with the ynet app also with Google and Cloudflare DNS with enabled DNS filter.

Ok, now please check with Google DNS, but without DNS filter. I want to figure out which filter module is causing the problem.

If the problem persists with the DNS filter turned off + Google DNS, try turning off the filters one by one to see which one causes the issue. Once you find the one causing the problem, let us know.

If the problem is caused by the DNS filter itself, open the filtering log, clear it, restart the ynet app, and if the problem occurs again, copy the blocked domains (you can try unblocking them one by one, if that's not too much trouble).

issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] This site DOES NOT contain sexually explicit material, otherwise use [NSFW-specific form](./new?template=bug_report_NSFW.yml);

### What product do you use?

Other ad blocker

### AdGuard version

uBlock Origin v1.55.0

### What type of problem have you encountered?

Website or app doesn't work properly

### Which browser(s) do you use?

other (specify in comment below)

### Which device do you use?

Desktop

### Where is the problem encountered?

https://tv.vg.no/ (probably geo restricted)

https://vg.no/i/762Qv8/

### Ad Blocking

AdGuard Base filter

### Privacy

### Social Widgets

AdGuard Cookie Notices filter

### Security

### Other

_No response_

### Language-specific

_No response_

### What Stealth Mode options do you have enabled?

_No response_

### Add your comment and screenshots

### Affected site:
`https://www.vg.no/`

### Issue:
Some videos won't load, due to a blocked cookie consent, which needs to be accepted first.

### Examples:
`https://tv.vg.no/` (probably geo restricted)

`https://vg.no/i/762Qv8/`

### Screenshots:
* **With blocked cookie consent:**

![filterissue-vg3](https://github.com/easylist/easylist/assets/9382674/6789847f-3b9f-406e-8229-fe4f33e35a7a)

* **After the cookie consent has been accepted:**

![filterissue-vg4](https://github.com/easylist/easylist/assets/9382674/cde055a1-3424-4015-94dc-a24059337ba8)

### Problem filter:
* **AdGuard Cookie Notices filter**

### Problem rule:
```
speisekarte.de,businessinsider.com,historyextra.com,finn.no,vg.no,aftenposten.no,tek.no,vglive.no,bt.no,telegraph.co.uk##div[id^="sp_message_container_"]
```

### Possible fix:
```
- speisekarte.de,businessinsider.com,historyextra.com,finn.no,vg.no,aftenposten.no,tek.no,vglive.no,bt.no,telegraph.co.uk##div[id^="sp_message_container_"]

+ speisekarte.de,businessinsider.com,historyextra.com,finn.no,aftenposten.no,tek.no,vglive.no,bt.no,telegraph.co.uk##div[id^="sp_message_container_"]
```

### Other problem filters:
* ~~**EasyList - Cookie Notices** https://github.com/easylist/easylist/issues/18245/~~ _**(FIXED)**_
~~`||cmp.vg.no^`~~

* **I don't care about cookies** **_(NOTIFIED)_**
```
/wrapperMessagingWithoutDetection.js$domain=vg.no|boerse.de|bt.no|liberation.fr

cmp.$domain=telerama.fr|courrierinternational.com|vodkaster.com|svd.se|histoire-et-civilisations.com|malservice.aftonbladet.se|vg.no|tv.nu|tek.no|finn.no|pent.no|godt.no|aftenposten.no|omni.se|e24.no|helthjem.no|minmote.no|aftenbladet.no|klart.se
```

### Temp fix:
~~`vg.no#@#div[id^="sp_message_container_"]`
`@@||cmp.vg.no^`
`||cmp.vg.no^*/metrics/$important`~~

### Updated temp. fix (for uBO):
Until everything has been resolved, this should cover the current issues for all of the mentioned problem filters, in a more convenient way:
```
vg.no##div[id^="sp_message_container_"]
cmp.vg.no##+js(trusted-click-element, .btns-container > button[title="Tilpass"])
cmp.vg.no##+js(trusted-click-element, .message-row > button[title="Avvis alle"], , 2000)
@@||cmp.vg.no^
||cmp.vg.no^*/metrics/$important
@@||privacy-mgmt.com/mms^$domain=vg.no
```
(Credit for the above `##+js` rules goes to **piquark6046**)

--

### System info:
* OS/version: Windows 10 Pro 22H2 (x64)
* Browser/version: LibreWolf v121.0-1 (x64) [Tracking Protection = Standard]
* Adblock Extension/version: uBlock Origin v1.55.0

### Privacy

- [X] I agree to follow this condition

comment.body:
Yeah, I don't use AdGuard, but I don't see how it can get away with blocking `/wrapperMessagingWithoutDetection.js` for Schibsted sites..

About four months ago, Schibsted introduced the worst cookie consent policy ever, which forces people into having to pay for privacy.
This actually resulted in the Norwegian Data Protection Authority filing a case against them!

In order to properly bypass Schibsted's cookie consent, '**uBlock filters - Cookie Notices**' has a complex set of rules in place.
Blocking `/wrapperMessagingWithoutDetection.js`, or the popup that I mentioned in my previous post, completely breaks those rules!

'**uBlock filters - Cookie Notices**' clearly states that it's "**optimized for uBlock Origin, to be used with EasyList's and/or Adguard's "Cookie Notices" list(s)**"
..so IMO; it should contain the fix that I suggested!

comment.body:
Ok, reproduced on another device. It seems only unblocking `@@||googleads.g.doubleclick.net^` in DNS user rules will help.

Fixed for the case when `googleads.g.doubleclick.net` is not blocked by DNS.
You may switch to non-filtering AdGuard DNS, enable DNS filter and add `@@||googleads.g.doubleclick.net^`.
Since regular filtering rules also target this advertising domain, it is unlikely that the ads will be unblocked (though this is not impossible in apps).

Problem powinien zostać rozwiązany w kolejnej aktualizacji filtrów (pewnie za jakie 1-2 godziny).
Jeśli nie chcesz czekać na aktualizację, dodaj proszę poniższą regułę do reguł użytkownika:
```
[$path=/tv]youtube.com#%#//scriptlet('json-prune', 'playerResponse.adPlacements playerResponse.playerAds playerResponse.adSlots adPlacements playerAds adSlots', '', '/https:\/\/www\.youtube\.com\/s\/player\/.*\/(?:tv-player-ias\.vflset\/tv-player-ias\.js|tv-player-ias-tcl\.vflset\/tv-player-ias-tcl\.js):/')
```

issue.body:
### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking)
[https://www.lalesbienne.com/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.lalesbienne.com%2F)

### Comment
> AdGuard's site report (reports.adguard.com/en/lalesbienne.com/report.html) lists lalesbienne.com in the category "Adult", so it is blocked by AdGuard DNS Family Protection. This is a false positive. Screenshot 1 shows the "Adult" category; screenshot 2 shows the site's About page.
> 
> Hello,
> 
> I'm writing on behalf of La Lesbienne (https://www.lalesbienne.com), an independent editorial journal documenting lesbian history, politics and culture. We publish long-form essays, reporting, book reviews, literary criticism and archival research, and we are currently applying for non-profit status in Estonia.
> 
> Visitors on filtered networks are being blocked from reaching the site. We believe the domain is uncategorized or has been automatically miscategorized, most likely because of the word "lesbienne" (French for "lesbian") in the domain name and because the site is new.
> 
> The site contains no sexually explicit, pornographic or adult material. It is an editorial publication comparable to a literary or current-affairs magazine. Several filtering vendors have already reviewed it and categorized it accordingly: Forcepoint and OpenText BrightCloud as News and Media, and Symantec as Society/Daily Living.
> 
> We request that lalesbienne.com and www.lalesbienne.com be categorized as News & Media (secondary: Arts & Culture or Education), and that any adult, mature, sexuality-related or uncategorized/new-domain classification be removed. Our editorial scope is described at https://www.lalesbienne.com/about.
> 
> Thank you for your review.
> 
> Kay
> Business Manager, La Lesbienne
> `kay@lalesbienne.com`

issue.body:
# ATTENTION

> [!NOTE]  
> YouTube changes their detection scripts regularly. That means that sometime you can face the detection message.
> If all the following instructions do not work, please **email filters@adguard.com** or wait until any update is available. 

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use another adblocker in the same time because using another adblocker can delay/lags the YouTube loading (e.g., AdBlock Plus and AdBlock)[^1] OR interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use an userscript related to the bypassing YouTube detection message like [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing).
> Recently, YouTube anti-adblock script added infinite dummy advertisements to try to neutralize the userscript. ( [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing#264](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing/issues/264) )

> [!WARNING]
> Please check that there no another web browser extension that has adblocking feature is enabled on your web browser. It can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> Saving memory feature of your web browser or sleep feature of your operating system can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.
> In this case, please re-enable AdGuard's filtering by toggling the protection toggle.
> Following the instructions can be needed.

### The instructions
1. Force to update the filters by clicking the reload button in AdGuard Browser Extension/AdGuard mobile or update tray menu in your system tray. [^2]
2. Reload the YouTube webpage without cache by pressing <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd> [^3].
3. Clear cache, cookies and site data of your web browser.
4. Re-open your web browser completely (checking your system monitor[^4] will be better).

[^1]: https://gitlab.com/adblockinc/ext/adblockplus/adblockplusui/-/issues/1576
[^2]: [AdGuard for Windows](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-windows/overview/#tray-menu); [AdGuard for Mac](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-mac/overview/#updates-check); 
[^3]: On macOS, <kbd>Command</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd>
[^4]: Task Manager on Windows, System Monitor on GNOME Shell, KDE System Guard on KDE Plasma or Activity Monitor on macOS. 


Previous issue https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/198973
